title: Conflict-induced hunger and Security Council authority

public.text: On 24 May 2018 the Security Council adopted draft S/2018/492 unanimously as Resolution 2417. The Netherlands spoke for co-penholders Côte d’Ivoire, Kuwait, the Netherlands and Sweden.
The Council condemned the use of civilian starvation as a method of warfare and the unlawful denial of humanitarian access.

delegate.source: S/PV.8267, p. 2, Netherlands for the four co-penholders
delegate.text: Speaking for the four co-penholders, the Netherlands described tools the Council could consider. These included sanctions, where appropriate, against those who deny humanitarian access unlawfully or starve civilians.

The United States encouraged the Secretary-General to warn the Council proactively about conflict-related famine conditions and said it looked forward to more regular, continuous reporting in the context of country-specific situations.

Russia argued that food insecurity also reflects factors outside armed conflict, including natural disasters and unilateral economic restrictions. It said the broader food-security problem extended beyond the Security Council's scope.

clause.text: Paragraph 9 recalls that the Council has previously adopted and may consider sanctions, where appropriate and consistent with existing practice, against individuals or entities obstructing the delivery of, access to, or distribution of humanitarian assistance.

Paragraph 11 asks the Secretary-General to continue regular country-specific reporting on the humanitarian situation and response, including famine and food-insecurity risk. Paragraph 12 separately requests swift reporting to the Council when the relevant risk arises in armed conflict.

comparisons.text: The co-penholders described possible Council tools. Paragraph 9 specifically recalls possible sanctions for obstruction of assistance under existing practice. It imposes no new sanctions.
The US expectation of more regular reporting is a national position. The resolution continues existing regular reporting and separately calls for swift alerts when the conflict-related risk arises.
